To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
smoking by pregnant women decreases infant birth weight, irrespective of gender, but increases childhood weight growth especially among male children.
maternal smoking during pregnancy decreased the birth weight of both male and female children but increased the childhood weight gain of male children only.
smoking by pregnant women decreased birth weight in both male and female children but increased weight gain in male children during the childhood.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the gender differences in childhood growth trajectories after maternal smoking during pregnancy.
the effects of smoking by pregnant mothers on the growth of their children.
the association of maternal smoking with the childhood growth trajectory of children born to the mothers who smoked during pregnancy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
maternal smoking during early pregnancy is associated with increased childhood BMI in males, whereas the association is weak in females.
maternal smoking during pregnancy is related to childhood weight gain in males.
maternal smoking during pregnancy increases the risk of overweight and obesity among the male children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of maternal smoking on fetal growth and subsequent childhood weight gain is different by gender.
maternal smoking during pregnancy is associated with the gender difference in the childhood growth trajectory, which may be due to the sex difference of the effects of maternal smoking on the fetus.
the male children of the smoking mothers were more vulnerable to the effects of smoking than the female children.
The main takeaway from our work is that
smoking by pregnant women decreases infant birth weight irrespective to gender but increases childhood growth, especially in male children.
smoking by pregnant women increases childhood growth in male offspring but not in females.
maternal smoking during pregnancy decreases the birth weight irrespective of the gender, and increases the weight gain in the male offspring after 3 years old.
